The '''Lightspeed Panthers''' were a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] [[Fighter wing/Legends|wing]] of [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighters]] who served the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. They were famed for their decorative [[Tooth/Legends|fang]]-jawed nose art that adorned their fighters.<ref name="EGTW" />

Equipped with [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom Corporation]] T-65 [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing starfighters]], the Lightspeed Panthers performed with distinction during the [[Fei Hu campaign]], [[Death/Legends|destroying]] at least 286 [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighters]] during the first nine [[Standard month/Legends|months]] of the engagement, while the Lightspeed Panthers only lost four [[Starship/Legends|craft]]. The success of the Lightspeed Panther's efforts&mdash;along with the overall success of the T-65 during [[Starfighter combat/Legends|combat]] engagements&mdash;forced the Empire to respond by introducing the [[Lancer-class frigate/Legends|''Lancer''-class frigate]] and [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN interceptor]] starfighter in an attempt to level the battlefield and prevent one-sided campaigns such as the one at [[Fei Hu sector/Legends|Fei Hu]].<ref name="EGTW" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The 'Lightspeed Panthers,' with their snazzy nose art and devastating kill ratio, are a direct reference to the Flying Tigers of World War II ''[&hellip;]''|Paul Urquhart|<ref name="Endnotes">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/24614452839/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-10|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 10|date=2012-06-07}}</ref>}}
The Lightspeed Panthers were mentioned in the reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', written by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]<ref name="EGTW" /> and released on [[April 3]], [[2012]].<ref name="Penguin">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/180097/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-star-wars-by-jason-fry-with-paul-r-urquhart|text=The Essential Guide to Warfare: Star Wars}}</ref> On [[June 7]], 2012, Fry posted a statement from Urquhart on Tumblr as part of the [https://jasonfry.tumblr.com/post/24614452839/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-10 tenth part] of a series of endnotes for ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' in which Urquhart revealed that the Lightspeed Panthers were a direct reference to the [[Wikipedia:Flying Tigers|Flying Tigers]],<ref name="Endnotes" /> a group of volunteer [[Wikipedia:Americans|American]] pilots who fought for the [[Wikipedia:Republic of China Air Force|Chinese Air Force]] during [[Wikipedia:World War II|World War II]].<ref name="Npr">{{WebCite|url=https://www.npr.org/2021/12/19/1062091832/flying-tigers-americans-china-world-war-ii-history-japan|text=The Flying Tigers: How a group of Americans ended up fighting for China in WW II|author=James Doubek|date=2021-12-19|work=[[Wikipedia:NPR|NPR]]|archivedate=20230306222602}}</ref> The Flying Tigers were also noted for their high kill ratio and the teeth [[Wikipedia:Nose art|nose art]] on their planes,<ref name="Endnotes" /> though the art on the Flying Tigers' planes depicted shark teeth.<ref name="Npr" /> Urquhart also noted the similarities between the T-65s of the Lightspeed Panthers and the [[Wikipedia:Curtiss P-40 Warhawk|P-40 Warhawks]] of the Flying Tigers, stating that they were both pilot-friendly multi-role fighters.<ref name="Endnotes" />
